title: Renew the old
hook: Rav Kook taught that the old should be renewed and the new made holy
carry: renew the old, bless the new
tomorrow: can a hope for gentleness reach all the way to the animals?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the inner rooms where God weeps, and the strength of weeping with someone. God weeps with us. Today, a teacher who wouldn't choose between old and new.

A grandmother's recipe card, splattered and soft at the corners, gets photographed and texted to the whole family, then made with oat milk because a cousin can't do dairy. Old and new, on one stovetop. Rabbi Abraham Isaac Kook, known as Rav Kook, a rabbi and mystic in the Land of Israel, answered the question in one short Hebrew line: ha-yashan yitchadesh, ve-he-chadash yitkadesh. The old will be renewed, and the new will be made holy.
screen: `A RECIPE CARD, TEXTED TO EVERYONE.` → `OLD AND NEW ON ONE STOVETOP.` → `THE OLD RENEWED, THE NEW MADE HOLY.`

segments.voice: So, what do you do with something old that still matters? Rav Kook's answer runs both ways. The old doesn't get frozen behind glass or thrown out; it gets renewed, made alive again for new people in a new time. And the new doesn't get feared or swallowed whole; it gets made holy, lifted up and given a place. He refused to choose between the house of study and the changing world outside it. Now a neighbor tradition, in its own words. In the Gospel of Matthew, Jesus ends a run of parables with a picture. In the King James Version, every scribe instructed unto the kingdom of heaven "is like unto a man that is an householder, which bringeth forth out of his treasure things new and old." A house with a treasure room, and someone who knows when to bring out each thing. Here's the shared ground: neither one picks only the old or only the new. Both trust a person to carry the two together. And the honest difference. Rav Kook speaks of the Torah's life renewed among his own people. In Matthew the treasure is the teaching of the kingdom of heaven, which Christians hear as the teaching of Jesus. And the verbs differ. Matthew's householder brings things out as they are. Rav Kook asks that both be changed: the old renewed, the new made holy.

segments.voice: Find one old thing within reach that still matters: a worn book, a tool, a photo, a mug from someone you love. Give it one small act of renewal during the sit: wipe it clean, smooth a page, set it where you'll see it. As you do, ask what new day it could belong to.
